info:
Japanese does not have a dedicated future tense. The polite です/ます non-past form can describe either present or future, with context indicating the time.

行きます = I go / I will go
明日行きます = I will go tomorrow

The extra particles are not future markers. They show the relationship between the verb and other words:

を = direct object: パンを作ります = make bread
に = destination/location/recipient: 学校に行きます = go to school
と = with: 彼女と行きます = go with her
にいる = be somewhere (person/animal)
にある = be somewhere (thing)

Important future constructions:

〜つもりです = intend/plan to
〜でしょう = probably/will likely
〜なければなりません = will have to / must
potential form = will be able to
native_answer: I will get a gift.
answer: 私はプレゼントをもらいます。

にある = be somewhere (thing)

Important future constructions:

〜つもりです = intend/plan to
〜でしょう = probably/will likely
〜なければなりません = will have to / must
